findings.rationale: The role's trust policy lets any in-account principal assume it, and it carries AdministratorAccess: assumption is privilege escalation, not a configuration detail.
A standing policy grants sts:AssumeRole on the administrator role, so every principal holding the policy holds a documented path to admin.
The trust policy admits a principal from a different account outright; the identity boundary is the other account's controls, not this one's.

findings.control: identity boundary: MFA condition on sensitive trust
findings.rationale: The trust statement carries no MFA condition, so a compromised external principal needs nothing beyond its long-lived credentials to assume the role.
